title: The Pyrenoid: a Rosetta Stone for Tackling Five Unsolved Problems in Cell Biology
content: Modern cell biology grapples with fundamental questions about how life builds and regulates itself, from the control of organelle size to the coordination of metabolic pathways. Here, I propose that the algal pyrenoid, a phase-separated membraneless organelle central to global carbon fixation, can serve as a Rosetta Stone. Coupled with generative artificial intelligence, this single model system provides a platform to dissect these long-standing problems through the lens of an emerging paradigm called Generative Science. This approach moves beyond analyzing what exists to designing and building novel biological systems to uncover fundamental rules. The pyrenoid is uniquely suited for this, as its simple, programmable "sticker-spacer" grammar is amenable to an inverse design approach. I will outline how this system can be transformed into a living laboratory to tackle five of cell biology's great unsolved problems: (1) scaling of organelle size, (2) organelle communication and metabolic channeling, (3) biophysical basis of condensate function, (4) mechanism of de novo organelle biogenesis, and (5) cellular-planetary co-evolution. This "build to understand" methodology offers a tangible path to transforming cell biology into a truly quantitative and predictive science.
